.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (delivery profile, verdicts, evidence standard, known false positives)

qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/raw-evidence-index.json (re-hashed run_golden.sh, tests/functional.cjs, app.js and seed_data.json; all match); qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/tests/functional.cjs:448,454,492
evidence: Achievability: every capability is reachable. environment/Dockerfile installs node:22, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally with NODE_PATH, copies /instructions and /assets, and creates /app. integration.md states the start path, port 3000, DB_PATH, health route, seed import, fixed clock and no-symlink rule, and the network is public. Every seeded fact the criteria rely on exists in environment/assets/seed_data.json, and the retention arithmetic agrees with the brief. K-10 at 2026-05-05T11:00:00Z is exactly 7 days old (walls-and-retention.md:23 'a message sent exactly seven days ago on a seven-day matter is already gone'), and K-11, one second younger, survives. K-1 (11 days) is gone while its replies K-14/K-15 survive. Held K-17 is overdue on release. K-13 (8 days, versions 2,400->4,200) dies when M-13 goes to 7 days, while held K-7 stays. K-2 is held with an earlier version. Accounts, roles, Dev's M-12 wall, timer options and read_up_to match the brief and app_context. Most demands have one reasonable reading: walls on every route with a plain 'not available', partner-only timers and holds, Harriet-only walls, hold scope, idempotent resend, order of same-timestamp messages, transcript contents, case-insensitive search, the refusal reason in place, and 390 px. AMBIGUITY 1 (defect): the criteria grade the thread's sent time and its time zone, but the brief states neither. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:216 (sent_once_in_order, weight 2.5, parts conjunctive) requires 'Each shows the firm's fixed sent time: 11:00 in the thread (a date there is optional) and 2026-05-12 11:00 in the transcript'. judge.toml:243 (search_and_transcript, weight 2.5) requires the transcript heading 'generated time 2026-05-12 11:00'. The public notes say only, at integration.md:7, 'The firm runs on a fixed clock, 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z. New messages, edits and transcripts carry that time', and at walls-and-retention.md:35 that the transcript lists each message's 'sent time'. Nothing says the thread must display each message's time, or that times are shown in UTC. 'Carry that time' reads naturally as the stored timestamp. The golden prints UTC with a 'UTC' suffix (solution/app/public/app.js:56 fmtTime), and the scripted harness asserts '2026-05-12 11:00' (qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/tests/functional.cjs:448,454,492), so the golden's choice became the grade. tests/app_context.md:28 'Times shown may use any clear format' covers neither a different zone nor a missing time. AMBIGUITY 2 (Note, low): conversations.md:13 'links to http or https addresses that open in a new tab' most naturally means auto-linking bare addresses, which is what judge.toml:176 checks with 'https://example.org/lease'. A reader could instead implement only [text](url) link syntax, mirroring the explicit *bold*, `code` and '> ' syntaxes listed beside it. That fails the positive control. AMBIGUITY 3 (Note, low): conversations.md:9 refuses an edit saved 'from a page that is out of date, because the message changed since they opened it', and conversations.md:31 makes live edits reach open tabs within five seconds. judge.toml:161-163 keeps the second context's edit box open past that live update. An app that rebases the open editor on the live update would accept the stale save, though 'since they opened it' supports the criterion. Mark-unread semantics (conversations.md:25 'moves the line there') agree with judge.toml:201 (count 1, line above JUDGE-U2). No unreachable item was found.
counterexample: Take a conforming app for this UK firm (Welsh staff names, figures in pounds) that formats times with Intl.DateTimeFormat in Europe/London. It shows '12:00' (BST) in the thread and '12 May 2026, 12:00 BST' on the transcript. That fails sent_once_in_order (2.5) and search_and_transcript Part B (2.5), about 5/33.5 of functional weight, or roughly 9% of reward. Equally conforming apps might show 'just now' in the thread, or show no per-message time there and keep sent times in the transcript as walls-and-retention.md:35 asks. Those fail sent_once_in_order Part B and so also lose the idempotency credit in Part A. Each app follows every public sentence and stores 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z correctly. This is a false negative for a conforming app. No broken app passes because of it.
suggested_fix: Add one sentence in the requester's voice to integration.md, e.g. 'Show times as the clock gives them, in UTC, and show each message's sent time in the thread as well as in the transcript.' Otherwise, relax judge.toml:216 and :243 to accept the same instant in any clearly labelled zone and drop the thread-time demand. Optionally say in conversations.md:13 that bare http/https addresses become links.
